environment.browser: Codex In-app Browser (exact engine version unavailable)
environment.dpr: not exposed by the safe Browser evaluation scope

contract.outcome: Characterize legacy FlyingLines worker scalability without changing animation semantics.
contract.primary_metric: Median worker animation callback duration across three windows.
contract.secondary_metric: Median worker rAF interval and approximate cadence.
guardrails: worker-reported particle count matched requested count
contract.materiality: Not applicable: descriptive baseline, no candidate/adoption decision.

probe.clock: worker performance.now() and worker rAF timestamp
probe.callback_scope: legacy effect loop callback: simulation/update plus Canvas2D render
probe.observer_effect: One performance.now pair per frame, bounded arrays, and one worker-to-main log message per 60 sampled frames; opt-in only.

pilot.reason: 300/500-particle windows did not complete within the initial bounded wait; final workload was rerun from scratch with 30/60.

observations: 100 particles stayed near the 120 Hz presentation interval.
300 particles had a roughly 24 ms median callback and roughly 25 ms median frame interval.
500 particles had a roughly 67.5 ms median callback and roughly 67 ms median frame interval.
Callback growth closely tracks unique pair-count growth across the three sizes.

inference.hypothesis: Quadratic pair work is the dominant scalability constraint in this workload.
inference.support: 100→300 pair count grows 9.06x while callback median grows 8.57x; 100→500 pair count grows 25.20x while callback median grows 24.11x.
limitations: Render work and number of accepted connections are included in callback duration.
Probe overhead was not independently subtracted.
This is a baseline, not an optimization A/B.

adoption_decision: None. Phase 6 will compare brute-force and spatial-index candidates against a deterministic oracle and this lineage.
